en.title: German political developments: Ukraine credit talks and domestic policy
en.dek: German Chancellor Merz faces resistance on Ukraine financing; domestic budget talks produce tax measures but no spending cuts.
facts: Friedrich Merz proposed using frozen Russian assets to secure a billion-euro credit for Ukraine, but the European Council rejected the plan in December 2025.
Robert Fico of Slovakia called Merz' proposal 'from the textbook of extortion' and said Slovakia would never support a loan to Ukraine.

Andrej Babis of the Czech Republic said the EU budget and Ukraine funding have 'nothing to do with each other' and noted 100 billion euros are already earmarked for Kyiv, though not available until 2028.
Péter Magyar of Hungary declined to comment on Merz' initiative while standing next to the Chancellor in Berlin, saying he does not think it is the right direction.
German coalition negotiations produced a budget agreement that includes new taxes on alcohol, sugar, and tobacco, but ruled out cuts to parental or housing benefits.
body: Friedrich Merz has proposed drawing on frozen Russian state assets to secure a multi-billion-euro credit for Ukraine, but the plan has run into resistance from several EU member states. At a Dublin meeting, Robert Fico of Slovakia called Merz' move 'from the textbook of extortion' and said his country would never support a loan to Ukraine.

Andrej Babis of the Czech Republic said the EU budget and Ukraine funding are separate issues, noting 100 billion euros are earmarked for Kyiv but will not flow until 2028, while the Ukraine needs 70 billion more next year with the EU covering two-thirds.

The Hungarian prime minister Péter Magyar declined to comment on Merz' initiative while standing next to the Chancellor in Berlin, saying he does not think it is the right direction. Diplomats close to Germany question whether Merz could have secured a better outcome by engaging partners privately rather than publicly pressing four countries into a corner.

German coalition negotiations late on Wednesday produced a budget agreement that includes new taxes on alcohol, sugar, and tobacco, but ruled out cuts to parental or housing benefits. The deal was reached after hours of bargaining between CDU, CSU, and SPD faction leaders, who went to the press just before midnight.
en.context: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is pushing to use frozen Russian assets to fund a Ukraine credit, but faces opposition from Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Bulgaria. At the same time, Germany's coalition is negotiating a 2027 budget.
en.imageCaption: Die Wirtschaftsweisen fordern die Bundesregierung auf, Subventionen und Sozialausgaben zu kürzen. Die Verteidigungsausgaben müssen künftig aus dem regulären Haushalt statt über Kredite finanziert werden. Andernfalls laufen die Staatsschulden aus dem Ruder.

Fehlanzeige' and 'neue Alkopop-Steuer, eine Zuckersteuer und eine höhere Tabaksteuer' as things that were NOT done), 'no cuts to parental or housing benefits' is not in S4 (S4 says Kürzungen beim Eltern- oder Wohngeld? Bloss nicht — the final outcome is not stated), 'budget agreement' implies a deal was done but S4 describes a 'Document des Scheiterns', 'hours of bargaining' and 'just before midnight' are not in S4, 'Chancellor Friedrich Merz had pushed for lower electricity tax' is not in S4 (S4 mentions Merz quote about electricity tax but not that he pushed for it in negotiations), 'Throm called for better integration and faster deportations' is from S3 but the body sentence about 'when origin countries deny Aufnahme' is not in S3; S3 only says Throm calls a way for Rückführungen when Herkunftsländer die Aufnahme verweigern', 'context' section contains claims not in sources (e.g. 'Germany's coalition is negotiating a 2027 budget that will include new consumption taxes')
